title: Simplicial mapping components compute localized morphisms
statement: Use model categories, weak factorization systems, functorial factorizations, cofibrant and fibrant objects as defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test], simplicial tensors and cotensors as defined in [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor], and the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Enlarge universes so the categories and localizations below exist as ordinary categories. A simplicial model category means a model category enriched, tensored and cotensored over simplicial sets, in which for each cofibration $a:A\to B$ and fibration $p:X\to Y$ the corner map $\operatorname{Map}(B,X)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,X)\times_{\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)}\operatorname{Map}(B,Y)$ is a Kan fibration, trivial if $a$ or $p$ is weak. Let $\mathcal M$ be a simplicial model category. Write $q:\mathcal M\to\mathcal L=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$ for the ordinary category obtained from finite composable strings of ordinary arrows and formal inverses of weak equivalences, modulo the composition, identity and inverse relations. Assume the ordinary bifibrant localization and saturation conclusions of [lem-coef-simplicial-bifibrant-localization]. For every cofibrant $P$ and fibrant $Y$, sending a vertex $f:P\to Y$ to $q(f)$ induces a bijection $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(P,Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal L}(qP,qY)$. This bijection is natural for all actual arrows between cofibrant sources and between fibrant targets, and respects composition whenever both the source and target conditions hold. It is the bijection induced by the actual localization functor, not merely an abstract bijection of sets.
